It is also important for people who have debts such as mortgages or student loans, as these debts will continue to accrue even if the individual is unable to work.  There are different types of disability insurance, including short-term and long-term disability insurance. Short-term disability insurance typically provides benefits for a shorter period of time, such as a few months, while long-term disability insurance provides benefits for a longer period of time, such as several years or until retirement age. It is important to carefully consider the type of disability insurance that is best suited for your needs and financial situation.  It is also important to note that the cost of disability insurance can vary depending on factors such as your age

query: what would happen if we expanded unemployment benefits
generator_output: Expanding unemployment benefits would provide more financial support to jobless workers during a period of high unemployment. The CARES Act, passed in March 2020, included a robust expansion of unemployment benefits, including an additional $600 per week for up to four months, an extension of benefits for those who have exhausted their state benefits, and expanded eligibility to previously ineligible groups such as gig workers and freelancers. This expansion was intended to be a temporary measure and was set to expire in July 2020.  Since then, there has been debate in Congress about whether to extend the $600 weekly unemployment boost. The HEALS Act, a proposal introduced by Senate Republicans in July 2020, does not extend the $600 boost, instead offering a much more austere across-the-board $200/week through September. Starting in October, the proposal would leave it up to states to supplement their usual unemployment benefits with extra federal unemployment to total 70% of someone's lost wages, with a cap of $500. However, not everyone may get 70% of their wages replaced due to the cap.  It is unclear at this time whether Congress will pass a new stimulus bill that includes an extension of the unemployment boost. If a new bill is approved, it would need to be passed by both the House and Senate
